utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, you may proceed with calling the case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the case number, IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin and Momir Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin, good afternoon to you. Can you hear me in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I can hear you and I understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. I see that General Talic is already at attention. Good afternoon to you. Can you hear me in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED TALIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, General Talic. You may sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Joanna Korner, Andrew Cayley, assisted by Denise Gustin, case manager. Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you. Appearance for Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. I'm John Ackerman. I'm with Milan Trbojevic and Marela Jevtovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And good afternoon to you. And appearances for General Talic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Natasha Ivanovic-Fauveau for General Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And good afternoon to you too. Any interesting preliminaries?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, it depends on your definition of "interesting." One is, can I raise the timing aspect again, because we've arranged for a witness from the Kljuc municipality to be here to testify on Thursday. Now, I don't know whether we'd all forgotten or whether it was a new arrangement, but we're not sitting tomorrow until quarter to 4.00 on this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Tomorrow -- yeah, that's because I have -- I don't think it's quarter to 4.00. The -- the Status Conference in Nikolic I estimate will only last, I suppose, a few minutes. There is practically two very minor things. It's more of a procedural necessity than anything else. And I think it should be over in not more than half an hour. But then I am advised that they need another half an hour to prepare the Chamber -- or the courtroom for the next. So I reckon we should be ready by 3.15.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, what it said on the list -- I've been -- definitely was 15.45. But if Your Honour thinks 3.15 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would prepare -- everyone prepared for 3.15, maximum 3.30.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's just we've again been discussing how long this witness will take. Madam Fauveau will certainly take all of this afternoon's session and part of tomorrow's apparently. Mr. Ackerman, I don't know with the extra added half hour tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It's a little bit difficult to tell, Your Honour, but it appears that I would go through most of the next day if not all of it. So that would mean that I would have what was left of Madam Fauveau's time tomorrow plus probably all of the next day. I just don't know. It's -- I could finish quicker than that. It's difficult for me to tell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Tomorrow the situation -- the position is as follows, because I'm even saying 30 minutes. Basically there's nothing to discuss, because there is a pending judgement which is -- will not be handed down tomorrow but will be handed down pretty soon and we just have to make that known. And then make sure that the accused is -- is okay. Otherwise, I mean -- and there's a question of nothing else, basically. So it might also -- the last time it was over in 15 minutes, the last Status Conference. So this could well happen more or less in the same time. If you are prepared to cooperate to the extent to make yourself available, say, at even 3.00 and possibly try to start 3.00 tomorrow, that would save us some time and then we'll try and make an effort, all of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's fine. We can all -- we can all do that. Our only concern and we were talking about it before you came in, is we do not want to bring this second witness here and not finish him by close of business Friday. That's the thing we're concerned about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And it's a legitimate concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, yeah, it's definitely a legitimate concern.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it doesn't seem to me that we've really got much further. Given that we've got extra time, from what Your Honour is saying, an extra half hour, it looks like it's still worth keeping the witness. Because we'd have to stop the witness from coming now if there was a real prospect that this witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would agree to that, I mean, because that's -- today is Monday -- Tuesday --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ackerman's original estimate was about a session to cross-examine. That's why we got a shortish witness from Kljuc to come up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I would go for that --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I would -- I think from what I understand from Mr. Nicholls, who's going to be calling the witness, it should be fairly short. So I think we better try and do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Rather than wasting two days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The second matter, Your Honour, very briefly: By chance I was looking through an old transcript and saw a discussion about reciprocal disclosure so I thought I would just gently raise that again so that it's on the record, as the Americans are very keen on it, that we haven't had any documents for some time that the Defence propose to use. Mr. Ackerman in fact tells me that it's likely we'll be getting some in the near future, but I raise it so that it's a live issue again. And it's particular because Madam Fauveau proposes to use a document today which she assures us she's given to us in January, and I'm sure she's right. But it's not one that we've used before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. That, I suppose, has been taken note of by the two Defence teams and will be acted upon as and when necessary. I thank you. The members of the audience are going to be disappointed - only two - but it's still a disappointment because we will go into closed session now. So you will not be in a position to follow what's going to happen, the proceedings. In the meantime, the usher will bring forward the witness and Madam Fauveau --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I see -- is it -- do you require us to be in closed session? So we'll stay in open session for a while until Mr. Ackerman raises --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we've given to the registry today a packet of documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are still in closed session. Wait one moment, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. No it says open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now it's open.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: We've given a packet of documents which we've marked Exhibit DB94.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The usher can bring forward the witness in the meantime, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: DB -- DB 94. There's a series of documents and what these are, are the Dzonlic documents that were turned over to us by the Prosecutor. We've sent them to CLSS, they've been translated and now we've given them to the registry, and we'll just file them all as 94, Exhibit 94.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And we'll go into closed session once more, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: at 6.32 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 23rd day of July, 2002, at 2.15 p.m.
